sentences.text: The marriage between petitioner No.1 and respondent No.2 was solemnized on 10.3.2019 at Pimpri, Pune, Maharashtra and there is no child out of their wedlock.
After few months of the marriage, their life was distressed due to difference of opinion and domestic issues also started.

Thereafter, respondent No.2 lodged an FIR against the petitioners under Section 498A read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code and the proceedings are pending before the Court of learned Judicial Magistrate First Class, Raipur, Chhattisgarh bearing Criminal Case No.
5187 of 2020 (State of Chhattisgarh vs. Navin Aghicha and Ors.).

sentences.text: Respondent No.2 and petitioner No.1 moved an application dated 7.10.2022 under Section 320(2) and 320(8) of Cr.P.C. on the basis of amicable settlement for compounding the offence of Section 498A read with Section 34 of IPC registered by respondent No.2 herein against the petitioners.

In pursuance of the above-mentioned incidents, it is also pertinent to mention here that respondent No.2 and petitioner No.1 have also moved an application under Section 13(B) of Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 to obtain a decree of divorce by mutual consent.
3) Learned counsel appearing for the petitioners and respondent No.2 would submit that the dispute between the parties has already been settled.

They would further submit that the statement of the parties regarding settlement of the dispute has been recorded before the Registrar (Judicial)
of this Court on 8.8.2023, where they have categorically stated that they have settled the dispute and arrived at a settlement without any coercion, greed, or pressure.
4) Vide order dated 8.8.2023, petitioner No.1 and respondent No.2 were directed to appear before the Registrar (Judicial) for recording their statements.
In pursuance of the above order, petitioner No.1 as well as respondent No.2 appeared before the Registrar (Judicial) on 8.8.2023 and their statements were recorded.

5) Learned counsel for respondent No.2 would submit that statement of respondent No.2 has already been recorded before the Registrar (Judicial) on 8.8.2023 and as the parties have settled their dispute respondent No.2 does not want to pursue this criminal case furthermore against the petitioners and thus, the order for quashing of criminal proceedings pending before the Court of learned Judicial Magistrate First Class, Raipur bearing Criminal Case No. 5187 of 2020 against the petitioners, FIR No. 12 of 2020 and the entire charge- sheet (final report) bearing No. 57 of 2020 may be passed.
6) I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the documents.
7) The Hon'ble Supreme Court has held in the matter of 'Ramgopal And Another Vs State of Madhya Pradesh, reported in 2021 SCC Online SC 834' and 'Narinder Singh and Others Vs. State of Punjab and Another reported in 2014 (6) SCC 466', that the matters which can be categorized as personal in nature or in the matter in which the nature of injuries do not exhibit mental depravity or commission of an offence of such a serious nature that quashing of which would override public interest, the Court can quash the FIR in view of the settlement arrived at amongst the parties.
